title: Predicting transcriptional outcomes of novel multigene perturbations with GEARS
why_relevant: GEARS is a strong prior-art architecture explicitly designed to predict perturbation outcomes for unseen perturbed genes using a gene relationship graph—directly aligned with this competition’s transfer/generalization goal.
extracted_technique: Gene-graph-informed GNN with perturbation embeddings; message passing over a gene relationship graph to generalize to unseen perturbations; regularized training on perturb-seq data.
query: GEARS perturbation effect prediction graph neural network github
takeaway: Use a gene-graph inductive bias (or a lightweight diffusion approximation) when you need to generalize to unseen perturbed genes; keep strong regularization and metric-aware calibration to avoid cosine failures.

title: snap-stanford/GEARS (reference implementation)
why_relevant: Provides practical implementation details, training caveats, and dataset loaders that can inspire a Kaggle-friendly GEARS-lite pipeline or identify dependency risks (e.g., PyG).
extracted_technique: End-to-end GEARS training pipeline; reliance on PyTorch Geometric; notes on limitations and splits; processed loaders for Replogle K562/RPE1.
takeaway: If PyG is too brittle for Kaggle kernels, reimplement the minimal message-passing blocks in pure PyTorch and keep the model small; treat it as an optional upgrade over a strong low-rank baseline.

title: Deep-learning-based gene perturbation effect prediction does not yet outperform simple linear baselines
why_relevant: Warns that many deep perturbation predictors fail to beat properly constructed linear baselines; motivates a strong, calibrated low-rank/linear baseline as the default and a cautious upgrade path.
extracted_technique: Benchmarking guidance: build fair OOD splits and strong linear baselines; avoid baselines that trivially revert to zero for unseen perturbations; emphasize calibration and proper evaluation.
query: Deep-learning-based gene perturbation effect prediction does not yet outperform simple linear baselines Nature Methods 2025
takeaway: Prioritize a robust baseline (regularized low-rank / ridge with good embeddings + careful scaling) and only add deep graph/generative complexity if it gives consistent CV gains on the official metric proxy.

title: Replogle et al. 2022 processed Perturb-seq datasets (K562 genome-scale / essential; RPE1 essential)
why_relevant: Large K562 CRISPRi perturb-seq resource suitable for external pretraining of gene/perturbation representations to improve generalization to unseen perturbations in the target cell line.
extracted_technique: External pretraining on processed AnnData pseudo-bulk or single-cell perturbation signatures, then fine-tune on the competition’s 80 labeled perturbations and recalibrate for the metric.
query: Replogle 2022 CRISPRi Perturb-seq K562 dataset download processed data
takeaway: If external data is allowed and runtime permits, pretraining on K562 perturb-seq is the most direct way to lift performance on unseen genes; prefer pseudo-bulk signatures/embeddings to control size and time.
